title: Same model, up to rounding

blocks.text: GridCap's finance team rewrote the NPV calculation behind the objective. The new code discounts each year's benefit in a different order of multiplications, so a few coefficients now differ from the old builder's in the last binary digit, and it also creates variables in a different order. An exported-proto comparison calls every such pair of models different. The team wants a check that calls them the same model and still catches every real change.

Write `same_model(a, b, rel_tol=1e-9)` in `compare_models.py`. It compares two MathOpt models by name, so the order variables and rows were added in does not matter, and returns `True` when they state the same model:

items: the same variable names, each with the same bounds and the same integer flag;
the same row names, each with the same bounds and the same set of variables in its terms;
the same objective sense (maximize or minimize) and the same set of variables in the objective;
every coefficient, and the objective's offset, equal within a relative tolerance: use `math.isclose(x, y, rel_tol=rel_tol, abs_tol=0.0)`.

blocks.text: Names, bounds, integrality and sense are compared exactly: none of them comes from arithmetic that rounds. A variable that appears in one model's row and not in the other's is a difference, even if the other model would have given it a coefficient near 0. Read a model with `model.variables()`, `model.linear_constraints()` and `row.terms()`, and `model.objective` with its `is_maximize`, `offset` and `linear_terms()` (lesson 4.2.1). Run the file to see why exact comparison fails: `0.1 * 3 == 0.3` is `False` in floating point. About twenty lines.

cases.says: two models built in different orders are the same, and a changed coefficient makes them differ
coefficients that differ only by rounding count as equal, and a real difference does not
a term present in one model's row and absent from the other's is a difference
a variable that is integer in one model and continuous in the other is a difference
maximizing and minimizing the same expression are different models
a row whose bound differs is a difference

origin.section: A Fast Builder Is Correct Only If Its Exported Model Equals the Slow One's

concepts: comparing by name ignores build order, and coefficients from different arithmetic need a tolerance
